title: Global perfect maps detect vanishing on a quasi-compact open
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U be a quasi-compact open, and let K be in D_QCoh(X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Choose ambient and localized-open derived models in the same Hom universe. If for every perfect object P of D_QCoh(X) [def-pc-perfect-complex] and every beta:P→K the restriction beta|U is zero, then every stalk H^n(K)_x for n in Z and x in U is zero.

source.place: Tag 0E4G, Lemma 48.4.4, first paragraph; Tags 09IS and 09IM

proof.text: Choose a derived model on the open subscheme in the ambient Hom universe. Start with its standard derived category and apply the inverse over-site equivalence to the given slice-site derived category. Exact derived functoriality takes the equivalence counit to a composite isomorphism with identity, so the derived inverse is faithful. Mathlib locallySmall_of_faithful and hasLocalizationOfLocallySmall then supply the desired model. Choose its open models by the existing open-localization theorem.

U is qcqs. Restriction has quasi-coherent cohomology by the derived open restriction criterion. Apply the supported perfect generator with support all of U; its support conditions are vacuous, giving a perfect E whose shifted Hom groups detect zero.

Each shift E[n] is perfect: shift the local strictly perfect representatives, replace the bounds a,b by a-n,b-n, reindex the finite-free summands, and compose the derived restriction and quotient shift isomorphisms. For any alpha:E[n]→K|U, apply perfect map lifting with T=X, obtaining a perfect R, beta:R→K, and an inclusion i with i beta|U=alpha. Perfectness supplies quasi-coherence of R. The test hypothesis kills the slice-site restriction of beta. Naturality of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso transports this vanishing through the over-site equivalence, and hence alpha=0. The generator criterion therefore gives K|U=0.

Exact restriction commutes with homology. Thus each restricted homology sheaf is zero. The overFunctorEquiv identifies it with open-immersion restriction, and restrictStalkNatIso identifies its stalk at x with the original stalk. Applying the additive stalk functor gives the stated subsingleton.

lean.statement:
theorem perfect_open_support_detection
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ W : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over W))]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X)
    (htest : ∀ (P : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X), Scheme.IsPerfect X P.obj →
      ∀ β : P ⟶ K,
        (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
          U).mapDerivedCategory.map β.hom = 0) :
    ∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∈ U →
      Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K.obj).val.presheaf x))
